extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, patent attorneys, and Korean Intellectual Property Office examiners handling patent-related proceedings in the Republic of Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on legal capacity, representation, agents, and related procedural requirements under the Korean Patent Act, including who may file or be represented, agent powers, proof and survival of authority, ratification of defective acts, and treaty effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Capacity of Minors, etc. (Article 3(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: No minor person under limited guardianship, nor person under adult guardianship shall be able to file an application or a request or conduct any other proceedings relating to a patent unless represented by his/her legal representative: provided, however, that the foregoing shall not apply where a minor or a person under limited guardianship is able to engage in a legal act independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: cases where a minor or person under limited guardianship can perform a juristic act independently (acts merely acquiring rights, disposing of permitted property, carrying on special business permitted, representation, making a will, acting as member with unlimited liability, etc.). Note: a minor cannot conduct patent-related proceedings without consent of a legal representative even when represented by an agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Administrators for Overseas Residents (Article 5(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: No person with no domicile or place of business in the Republic of Korea (overseas resident) shall be able to conduct any patent-related proceedings or file legal proceedings ... unless he/she is represented by an agent who has a domicile or place of business in the Republic of Korea (patent administrator), except where the overseas resident sojourns in the Republic of Korea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an overseas resident conducts a patent-related proceeding without designating a patent administrator, an examiner shall give an opportunity for explanation and, if not addressed, return the documents. A patent administrator represents the principal in all patent-related proceedings and legal proceedings filed with respect to a disposition made by an administrative authority within the scope of authority empowered thereto (Article 5(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity of Foreigners to Hold Rights (Article 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: No overseas-resident foreigner shall enjoy a patent or any rights relating to a patent, except in any of the following cases: 1) where the foreigner's country allows nationals of the Republic of Korea similar rights; 2) where reciprocity applies when Korea allows the foreigner's nationals similar rights; 3) where allowed under a treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A foreigner with domicile or place of business in Korea shall enjoy patent rights regardless of reciprocity. Note explains treaty exceptions and practical consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and Scope of Patent-related Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent-related proceedings refer to filing of an application or a request or any other proceedings relating to a patent before the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office, an examiner, or the Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board, including: ① filing of an application; ② filing of a request/petition (request for examination, reexamination, petitions for trial, etc.); ③ other proceedings (requests for accelerated examination, deferral, technical evaluation, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions: proceedings carried out by the Commissioner (notifications, requests), internal examination processing (formality exam, classification, prior art search, substantive exam), proceedings before courts, administrative trials, ordinary public complaints, and warning procedures against third parties are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification of Proceedings by Persons Lacking Capacity (Article 7-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent-related proceedings conducted by a person who lacks legal capacity, the power of legal representation or the authority necessary shall have effect retroactively to the time when such proceedings are performed if ratified by the party involved when he/she has gained legal capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formality examination reveals a proceeding conducted by an incompetent, examiner shall order amendment within designated period; unless ratified within the period the proceeding shall be invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Power of Agent (Article 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agent empowered to conduct patent-related proceedings may conduct the following acts only if expressly authorized to do so: 1) convert, abandon or withdraw a patent application; 2) abandon a patent; 3) withdraw an application for registering extension of patent term; 4) withdraw a petition; 5) withdraw a request; 6) claim or withdraw a priority claim; 7) file a petition for trial under Article 132-17; 8) appoint a sub-agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These acts require express authorization in the agent's power; otherwise agent cannot validly perform them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Power of Agent (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who conducts a patent-related proceeding as an agent (including a patent administrator) shall prove his/her power in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners check power (e.g., Patent Net); where a representative is neither a patent attorney nor a legal representative, the examiner shall propose amendment and may treat unremedied proceedings as invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survival of Authority of Agent (Article 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority granted to an agent by a principal shall survive even in any of the following events: 1) principal’s death or loss of legal capacity; 2) corporate principal’s dissolution in merger; 3) termination of principal’s duty as trustee; 4) legal representative’s death or loss of legal capacity; 5) termination or change in legal representative’s authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent's authority continues through specified events; practical consequence is continuity of representation despite certain principal changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of Representation (Article 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a principal is represented by at least two agents, each of them shall independently represent the principal before the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or the President of the IP Trial and Appeal Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each agent may act separately unless otherwise limited; separate powers must be managed to avoid unauthorized acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders to Appoint or Replace Agents (Article 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commissioner or presiding judge finds that a person conducting proceedings is unable to properly perform the proceeding or to make a statement in oral hearings or is not fitted to perform the proceeding, he/she may issue an order to appoint an agent or to replace the agent; the Commissioner/presiding judge may order a patent attorney to represent the principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When ordering appointment/replacement, the Commissioner/presiding judge may completely or partially invalidate prior proceedings conducted by the person or agent before the office or board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation for Two or More Persons (Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more persons jointly perform a patent-related proceeding, each shall represent all, except for the following acts (which require joint action unless a representative is appointed): 1) convert/abandon/withdraw patent application; 2) withdraw application for extension registration; 3) withdraw a petition; 4) withdraw a request; 5) claim/withdraw priority; 6) file a petition for trial under Article 132-17. If they appoint a representative and notify the office/board, only the representative may act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment of representative must be proved in writing when notified. Without proper proof, acts may be invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview: Legal vs Contractual Representatives and Examiner Duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Representatives include legal representatives (empowered by law) and contractual representatives (power granted by principal). A contractual representative who is neither a patent attorney nor a legal representative is inadmissible to represent the patent applicant; the examiner shall check and propose amendment where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners verify representative status (e.g., number prefix for patent attorneys). Proceedings conducted by non-authorized persons may be invalidated if not remedied by amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Attorney Registration and Conduct Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent attorney shall engage in representation business before the IPO or patent courts only if registered; an unregistered patent attorney cannot carry out proceedings as a patent attorney and should be punished if they do. A patent attorney shall not handle a case previously handled as representative of the other party of the same case, and a person who is not a patent attorney shall not use the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations (handling disallowed cases or dual representation) are deficiencies for granting power of attorney; examiner shall order amendment and may invalidate proceedings if unremedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to Hold Rights by Juristic Person
rubrics_metrics.description: A juristic person obtains rights and obligations granted based on the Act, independent of its members. Where a juristic person conducts a patent-related proceeding, the name and the business address shall be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing company type (e.g., LLC to corporation) is treated as a change of name, not of holder; notification (Annex Form No.5) required to correct applicant code information. In rehabilitation/bankruptcy, custodian/administrator actions are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to Hold Rights by Nation or Local Government
rubrics_metrics.description: A nation shall serve as the holder of rights because it is deemed a juristic person. However, legislative, judicial, administrative branches, government-affiliated organizations, state-run research institutes, universities are not entitled to be a juristic person and cannot become holders of patent-related rights. Local governments are deemed juristic persons and can hold rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and limits for local government types are provided. If an applicant lacks capacity under Civil Act (e.g., a university), corrected naming or filing in the state's name is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity of Unincorporated Associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Associations without legal personality (clan gatherings, alumni meetings, churches, academies) in principle cannot conduct patent-related proceedings because of lack of capacity to hold rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: where such an association/foundation has a representative or an administrator, it can become a party for limited proceedings (request for examination, technical evaluation on utility models, opposition, trial, retrial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompetents: Definition and Practical Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'incompetent' includes 1) a person under age of 19 (minor), 2) a person adjudicated subject to limited guardianship, 3) a person adjudged subject to adult guardianship. An incompetent can conduct patent-related proceedings only when represented by a legal representative, subject to statutory exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acts an incompetent may perform independently are listed (Civil Act); note that proceedings by an incompetent require ratification or amendment as described under Article 7-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Treaty on Patent Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Treaties duly concluded and promulgated have the same effect as domestic laws (Constitution Article 6). Patent treaties (WIPO, Paris Convention, PCT, Budapest Treaty, Strasbourg Agreement) may be referred to for examination because some contain more detailed provisions than the Korean Patent Act (e.g., Paris Convention priority rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should apply treaty provisions where appropriate (e.g., recognizing priority from first application that was a utility model or design under Paris Convention even if Patent Act wording differs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Overseas Resident Filings Without Patent Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an overseas resident conducts a patent-related proceeding without designating a patent administrator, an examiner shall give him/her an opportunity for explanation and, if not addressed, return the documents to the overseas resident according to Article 5 of the Patent Act and Article 11 of the Enforcement Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical step: examiner must request remedy; failure leads to return of filing and no processing.
